summary: Clustered and attributed the frozen post-completion full-repository sweep (40587 passed / 979 failed / 117 errors) recorded by the predecessor Telegram-receipt IV phase. Independently confirmed src/pcae, scripts, pyproject.toml, and docs/contracts are byte-unchanged from the Telegram repair's production commit (8bfce890) through this phase's entry SHA, so the reproduction is source-byte-equivalent to the frozen original regardless of the exact historical SWEEP_SHA (not resolvable from durable local evidence -- pytest's nodeids/lastfailed caches merge across sessions and do not reliably pin an invocation time; no raw sweep log survives; recorded as bound to the byte-identical range rather than invented). Ran a full reproduction at this phase's entry SHA (python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider, single-process, no xdist): 1092 failed, 40538 passed, 24 skipped, 117 errors in 8831.59s -- errors match the frozen original exactly (117=117). Independently reconstructed the original invocation mode first: a bare pytest console-script run produces 15 collection errors (ModuleNotFoundError: no module named 'tests'/'prototypes'), all of which vanish under python -m pytest with zero other change -- classified environment/invocation-dependent, and confirms the original sweep used a python -m pytest-equivalent invocation (matching its exact 117-error count with no such collection failures). All 278 distinct failing/erroring files re-run individually in isolation: 68 files / 368 raw nodes collapse to 31 genuine failures when isolated (cross-test-order contamination, root cause unresolved but non-blocking -- dominant single case: 79 of the 117 total errors, 68%, from one fixture chain in the merged-RHAMP-mechanism test file where isinstance(root, HPACStoreAuthority) evaluates False only under certain full-suite collection orders; the same 125/125 tests in that file pass cleanly in complete isolation); 210 files / 841 raw nodes reproduce deterministically. All 16 N-16-5/F-5-priority files (RHAMP, FIDO2, PAWA, protected presentation, hpac_verifier, notifications/phase-reports, HATP Class-B topology -- 140 raw nodes) individually investigated with disposable fixed-SHA worktrees where needed: zero repair-attributable regressions, zero new blockers. Findings: (1) an already-disclosed/adjudicated hpac_verifier construction-boundary gap (HPAC-REQ-056, object.__new__ bypasses the isinstance-level seal) whose own test docstring states it is 'expected to FAIL against the current implementation' -- independently confirmed non-exploitable via the real Gate 5 consumption path, which never trusts isinstance and instead requires exact-object membership in the verifier's process-local registry plus fresh reverification (Gate 5 integration doc, explicit 'Forged (object.__new__)... -> authenticated_principal_not_verifier_issued' handling); (2) three historical-moving-authority self-checks (a frozen HMIC scope-list test superseded by a later deliberate widening in Phase 149O.20K.2, predating CAIR; two frozen git-diff-against-live-HEAD assertions from an earlier immutable repair phase, broken by CAIR's and TEL's own later, legitimate file changes -- the exact anti-pattern this repository's own F-3/F-4/F-6/F-7/F-9 family already names); (3) a stale recorded HMIC digest, independently reproduced as already-mismatching (with a different mismatching value) at the pre-CAIR baseline in a disposable worktree; (4) one phase_reports.py reconcile-rc failure, independently reproduced byte-identical at the pre-Telegram-repair baseline in a disposable worktree -- confirmed pre-existing, not repair-attributable. The remaining 194 non-priority files / 701 raw nodes were materiality-scoped per this phase's own governing rules; representative sampling of the largest clusters (HATP timestamp-canonicalization parser-domain tests, HPAC contract-freeze 'blocking finding' prose tests, a frozen production-file-allowlist test) confirmed the same historical/point-in-time and historical-moving-authority patterns, none touching N-16-5/F-5-relevant subsystems, none repair-attributable (e.g. human_approval_trusted_provenance.py last touched at Phase 149O.1H.5, long before this repair chain). Both prior repair verdicts (configured-agent-identity threading; durable Telegram acceptance receipt) remain INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED with no contradiction found. Generation-1 host state carried forward unchanged (not re-derived from live inspection; no failing test in the reviewed material set required it). No production or test file modified in this phase; no host mutation; no F-5 execution; no historical Telegram re-dispatch; no human/YubiKey/FIDO2 ceremony. VERDICT: FULL-REPOSITORY POST-COMPLETION SWEEP ATTRIBUTION: COMPLETE. F-5 CONTINUATION HOLD: CLEARED. N-16-5 remains NOT CLOSED; N-16-6/N-16-7 untouched.
